applicability.description: The repository owns automated logic that parses, compares, validates, or migrates byte-sensitive versioned artifacts across Git baseline, index, or worktree state.

requirements.statement: Clean tracked evidence comes from the exact verified HEAD regular blob, staged-only evidence from the exact stage-zero index blob, and unstaged or untracked evidence from the contained ordinary worktree file.
Repository evidence is acquired and passed to strict parsers as exact bytes without text pipelines, newline conversion, checkout-filter substitution, encoding inference, or normalization.
Conflicts, staged-plus-unstaged state, rename or copy state, deletion, missing required evidence, and any other ambiguous authority fail before evidence is accepted.
Git evidence must be a regular blob and worktree evidence must be an ordinary contained file; links, reparse points, non-regular entries, and escaping paths fail closed.
Evidence resolution is read-only and bounded, and an exact rerun over unchanged repository state returns the same source identity and bytes without changing repository state.
Automation may request maintainer review of this Semantic capability but does not rewrite, approve, mark ready, or merge consumer-owned semantic implementation.

conforming: Reviewed source-mapping evidence binds every supported clean, staged-only, unstaged, and untracked state to its owning Git or worktree byte authority and records fail-closed ambiguous states.
Executable anonymous-repository evidence proves exact bytes under checkout filtering, genuine noncanonical-byte rejection, containment, read-only behavior, and idempotent reruns.
Reviewed semantic handoff evidence confirms that automation writes only its transient review state and leaves consumer-owned semantic implementation to maintainers.
notApplicable: Reviewed repository evidence proves that no automated logic parses, compares, validates, or migrates byte-sensitive versioned artifacts across Git baseline, index, or worktree state.
The review identifies the inspected automation boundary and explains why byte-source selection cannot affect its evidence or decisions.
